subject: Post-demo recap, action grid & escalation map — PaciMed demo
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@pacimed.com>, Leah Kim <leah.kim@pacimed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap, immediate asks & proposed owners (PaciMed)

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — appreciate the candid feedback and the sharp questions. I wanted to capture the recap, surface the things we heard as decision gates, and list clear next owners so procurement/legal/security can move this along without back-and-forth.

Quick recap of what we covered:
- Scope: real-time triage + discharge-summary generation for ER flows (5k tokens avg).
- Run modes: hosted API initially, with Dedicated reserved pools as the target for steady state.
- ROI signal: 32% reduction in average physician note time in the pilot, potential $350k annual savings across 2 hospitals.

Stakeholders we identified (confirm/edit):
- Economic buyer: Alex Rivera (Clinical Ops) — evaluates cost/ROI and headcount impact.
- Security lead: Leah Kim (Infosec) — SOC2, data flows, KMS requirements.
- Procurement: Tom Perez — contract/PO and terms.
- Tech lead: Sophie Nguyen (Platform) — integration, API keys, network egress.

Decision criteria we heard from your side:
1) Latency: p95 generation < 450ms for 2k token workloads.
2) Data controls: VPC/private deployment option + KMS support for keys.
3) Auditability: per-request audit logs, retention 12+ months.
4) Contract/price: predictable committed throughput with overage caps.

Initial action grid (owners & target dates):
- SOW + pricing proposal (draft) -> Jordan Blake / Marissa Cole — target: 2027-03-18 EOD. (attachment: SOW_v1.pdf)
- Security requirements & evidence sheet -> Ben Carter / Karthik Iyer — target: 2027-03-16 (attachment: security_requirements.xlsx)
- Procurement intro & standard commercial terms -> Alex to introduce Tom Perez; Jordan to prepare buy-flow summary -> target: intro by 2027-03-15.

Immediate asks for PaciMed:
- Can you confirm the procurement contact (Tom?) and ideal PO timeline?
- Are there any non-starters in the decision criteria above? If latency targets need relaxing, flag now.

Attachments: SOW_v1.pdf (proposal draft), security_requirements.xlsx (initial evidence sheet). I've also dropped the HubSpot record and a small Drive folder of assets in the links below.

Next steps (my plan):
- Marissa & I will iterate SOW based on any commercial constraints you call out.
- Ben/Karthik will prepare a short packet for Leah: architecture diagram + sample audit logs (to satisfy SOC2 initial review).

Thanks — Jordan

--

- Procurement contact: Tom Perez (cc'd) — Tom will run the contract and PO process. Tom, timeline: our usual RFP window for projects above $100k is about 2 weeks if legal has no major redlines; procurement aims to have a PO issued by 2027-03-29 if all goes smoothly.

Tom — filing this in your queue.

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap, immediate asks & proposed owners (PaciMed)

Jordan — nice summary. Two refinements and one proposal from my side:

Refinements:
- "Auditability": clarify whether PaciMed expects per-token logs or per-request metadata only — that materially changes storage costs. Ben, can you validate storage/ingest pricing for both?
- "Latency": we can meet p95 < 450ms for 2k tokens on Dedicated for a committed pool; hosted API p95 will be in the 350-700ms range depending on load. I'll call this out explicitly in the SOW appendix.

Proposal (to reduce procurement friction):
- Offer a 3-month pilot commitment with a fixed committed throughput and a short "commercial guardrail" that caps overages at 20% per month; after pilot, transition to annual reserved capacity. This gives Procurement a predictable spend window and gives PaciMed a runway to validate the ROI signal.

Updated action grid (owners / explicit deliverables / due):
- SOW draft + cost appendix (100k/day vs 1M/day) -> Jordan + Marissa -> 2027-03-18 EOD. (deliverable: SOW_v1.pdf + cost appendix sheet)
- Security packet: architecture diagram (KMS details), sample audit log (redacted) -> Ben -> 2027-03-16 midday (deliverable: security_requirements.xlsx + audit_sample.log)
- Commercial term sheet & insurance/SLA summary -> Karthik -> 2027-03-17. (deliverable: term_sheet_redwood.docx)
- Procurement intro email template -> Jordan -> 2027-03-15 (to Alex/Tom).

Ben/Karthik — please ping me if any of the gating items look like they will slip; if so we will surface to Alex and propose the pilot guardrail above.

Thanks — Marissa
